results.content: President Trump's standing kept sliding by nearly every measure this week, though pollsters do not agree by how much. A Civiqs tracker put his approval at 34 per cent as of September 4; a Focaldata/Financial Times poll fielded through September 2 put it at 32 per cent, its lowest reading since that tracker began in May, with just 17 per cent approving of his handling of inflation and the cost of living. [...] points depending on tracker as of September 8 (Focaldata/Financial Times 32 per cent; Civiqs 34 per cent; Silver Bulletin 38.2 per cent; New York Times 38 per cent; RealClearPolitics average 39.6 per cent), a spread we carry in full rather than average.
